- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and forecast is falling, increase forecast slope to avoid premature pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast peak and add downward bias in next 5–7 days.  
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model often fails to recognize — adjust forecast to align with recent 10-day moving average.  
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome by >2% over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day to avoid overestimation.  
- If sentiment history shows no change (all 0.00), model should not assume trend continuation — use 10-day average as baseline for next forecast.  
- If true outcome drops sharply after a forecast peak, model often fails to adjust — apply lag correction: reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
